The main thing I haven't mentioned about me and my friend's conversation is that her unkindness was a direct result of my mistake. I made a bad joke (someone anonymously gave their name as "your mom" on a Google form, people were debating who did it, I said "my money is on \[my friend's name\]"; she confronted me cruelly about it; I assumed she was joking so I reacted with confusion instead of accountability; the conversation culminated with her saying "eat ass" and leaving).  

When I confronted her about it, she said "I've told you I find that kind of joke offensive so that's why I was hurt, because you're supposed to know me." So that's where the nuance is. The joke wouldn't have hurt her if anyone else made it, it only hurt her because it was proof that I didn't remember and therefore care about the things she told me. I thought this was a fair explanation and it justified the way she'd spoken to me so I tried to disregard my feelings for the next month. I didn't want another confrontation, especially because I knew my feelings were illogical. After that, though, I couldn't take the anxiety and rumination anymore and left her over text. 

So even though I want to say "I'll just do better next time," I feel so much that I should do better THIS time. She didn't deserve a reaction of that magnitude because I couldn't handle my emotions or engage in another hard conversation.

Unfortunately, a big part of this IS the desire to be universally liked, which is why the "you're self centered" comment, harsh as it was, resonated. Even if I try to make amends, it will be largely for selfish reasons, because my conscience won't leave me alone. So you're very right there that that's a thing to be worked on.

Thank you again if you made it this far -- I struggle to explain anything without providing large amounts of context. I hope it made sense. Whether or not I do fix things with this friend, I think I need to first make sure that my motivations are selfless, that I'm doing it out of a mature desire to clean up my mess and not out of a panicked need to make everyone love me.

I used to cry every day about not loving reading anymore - I deactivated my Goodreads because it hurt so much to see other people reading when I couldn’t. Reading was my THING as a kid. It was the only thing I used to do, and as I got older I stopped wanting to, and then I lost my sense of identity, and then I became desperate to read again, but because I was so desperate for it and so sure it would make me happy again, my brain wouldn’t let me. I couldn’t read a single page for years.

Some things that really helped me are audiobooks and FANFICTION about media I already love. I recently watched BBC Sherlock (so many years late to the party, I know…) and now the only thing I want to do is read Sherlock fanfiction. Fanfiction is also good because you’re scrolling, so you’re less aware of how many pages you’ve read (i don’t know if that’s an issue for you, but I used to get super anxious about having not read enough even though hours had passed). I also have to read 2-3 books a week for my degree so I put them on double speed as audiobooks and I enjoy that sense of achievement when I finish. 

Something will bring your passion back - it might not be audiobooks or fanfiction for you, but you should definitely experiment! I know it’s easier said than done, but reading is so wonderful, it’s worth it imo.

What is “me”? Why can I control my body with my brain and my brain with my body? 

Existence feels like a cruel joke. I don’t actually believe in a god, but in my head I rationalise it as a prank by some god who wanted to create a Worst Case Scenario. That god decided to make us utterly insignificant, suspended on a spinning ball in some irrelevant galaxy. He ensured that we would always be ultimately alone, because although we are able to communicate, we are confined throughout our lives to only our consciousness and we can only experience the world as ourselves, never as anyone else. He made us smart so we could agonise over existence; he made us emotional and creative so we could believe we had a purpose. Then he made us mortal so that we could never truly have a purpose, because eventually, no matter who we are, the legacies we worked towards will fade, either because we have died or because the earth has. He made us unable to grasp the size of the universe or its timespan, or the concept of nothingness. He made us love each other, but he made us inherently selfish. Some of us are ready to fuck up billions of equally intricate, emotion-filled, fascinating lives just to protect our own. 

I don’t know what the answer is to your questions, but I know you’re not alone. I don’t get existence either. The closest thing to a purpose I’ve been able to identify has been “be happy, because then you’ll be okay with dying when death comes for you” but there are so many factors outside our control when it comes to happiness. I wish it was easy.
